units.source_text: 歸根結底，訴諸他人終究都是徒勞。

en.t: In the end, appealing to other people is always futile.

units.source_text: 我只能不言真話，默默忍受，繼續搞笑。

en.t: All I could do was keep from telling the truth, endure in silence, and go on clowning.

units.source_text: 也許會有人嘲笑我：「什麼呀，你的言下之意是不相信人類嗎？

en.t: Perhaps someone would laugh at me and say, "What is this? Do you mean that you do not trust human beings?

units.source_text: 你什麼時候變成基督徒了？」

en.t: When did you become a Christian?"

units.source_text: 但我認為，對人類的不信任，未必就意味著我走向宗教之路。

en.t: But I think that distrust of human beings does not necessarily mean that I am turning toward religion.

units.source_text: 現在，包括嘲笑我的那些人在內，人類不都是彼此相互懷疑著，絲毫不把耶和華放在心裡，若無其事地活著嗎？

en.t: Even now, including those who would laugh at me, are not human beings all living calmly while doubting one another and giving no thought at all to Jehovah?

units.source_text: 同樣是我小時候的事，父親所屬政黨的一位名人來到我們鎮上演講，家中的男傭帶我去劇場聽。

en.t: This too happened when I was a child: a well-known figure from the political party my father belonged to came to our town to give a speech, and the male servants at home took me to the theater to listen.
